top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) credits one identifiable, mature empirical discovery: import competition and technological change produce large, persistent and uneven local labour-market adjustment costs, with job polarisation covered through Autor and Dorn (2013). The designs are transparent and have been re-run and challenged for over a decade. The core finding has held even though magnitudes and shift-share inference remain debated. Credit can be assigned exactly to these three, and the citation can be limited to empirical evidence without claiming the task-based theory of Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu and Restrepo. P002 (Katz in place of Dorn) is a close second. It has a defensible broader definition and rests on the older, better-confirmed wage-structure evidence, but its marginal credit is harder to separate from adjacent prizes and its boundary is more crowded. P003 (Melitz and Helpman) is a compact, mature discovery, but the priority claims of Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum and the welfare-gain critique can only be narrowed by wording. P004 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) is a credible, clearly attributed methods contribution with the narrowest evidence of changed understanding. I rank it above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile: no documented tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Katz, Melitz, Helpman, Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn. My field, political science, is closest to B040, which is not on the slate. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart, in a different department. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
